subject: Discovery follow-up — fit benchmarks, toolcall retries & JSON contract plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Morgan <danielle@brightdesk.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:10:00Z
Subject: Discovery follow-up — fit benchmarks, toolcall retries & JSON contract plan

Hi Danielle,

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn about BrightDesk's agent-assist workflow and the structured logging requirements for ticket enrichment. As promised, a concise follow-up with recommended next steps and an initial plan for the model-fit and structured-output evaluation: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary flow: agent submits a partial ticket + customer context -> model returns enrichment fields (priority, category, 3 suggested tags) + optional tool call to internal rules engine.
- Throughput target: 500 concurrent agents during peak (p95 latency target <= 300ms).
- Quality expectations: field-level accuracy > 92% on priority/category, JSON schema compliance mandatory.
- Data constraints: PII redaction required; retention policy 30 days.

Initial recommendations:
1) Models to try: Redwood-v2-small (quantized) for low-latency pass; Redwood-v2-medium for higher quality. We also recommend a head-to-head on a 1k sample using your prompt set to measure field-level F1.
2) Tool/function calling: use explicit JSON contract with strict validation on the server side. Include a retry policy: up to 2 retries for non-5xx errors, exponential backoff starting at 60ms, and fallback to a lightweight rule-based tagger on repeated failures.
3) Structured-output tests: we will run a JSON-schema validator during evals and instrument token-level traces to capture truncation or malformed responses.
4) KV-prefix caching: for repeated customer contexts we can cache last response to reduce latency for common patterns.

Attached: brightdesk_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts & expected outputs), and a short JSON contract draft (json_contract_v1.yaml). I'll push a short benchmark run (1k prompts) and a fit report by EOD tomorrow.

Next actions (proposed):
- You: confirm sample data delivery (anonymized) and a preferred window for the 1k run.
- Us (Redwood): run the model fit test, produce token-level regressions, and share the fit_benchmark_report_q4.pdf.
- Quick sync: 30 min follow-up the day after benchmark to review failures and agree on roll-forward (model or prompt fixes).

If that plan looks good I can schedule the run and loop in infra for throughput testing.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: brightdesk_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (44KB stub)
Attachment: json_contract_v1.yaml (3KB stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Morgan <danielle@brightdesk.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:08:00Z
Subject: RE: Discovery follow-up — fit benchmarks, toolcall retries & JSON contract plan

Thanks Vivek — adding a couple of operational checks we'll run during the fit: 

- Schema compliance suite: run against json_contract_v1.yaml; we'll surface field-level error rates and example failures.
- Retry correctness: instrument the call stack to tag retries (retry_count) and record outcome reasons (timeout, parse_error, model_error).
- Regression detection: compare token-level distributions and Exact Match on canonical examples. If we see a >3% drop in field accuracy from baseline we'll flag a quality regression.

Deliverables we'll share with BrightDesk:
1) fit_benchmark_report_q4.pdf — summary and per-field metrics (precision/recall/F1), latency percentiles, retry stats.
2) A curated prompt-fix list (CSV) for any systematic hallucinations or schema drift.
3) A short runbook for the fallback rule-based tagger and how to toggle it.

Also putting forward an evaluation cadence: initial fit (1k samples), targeted follow-ups on high-error buckets (200–500 samples) and then a 10k production-like run for throughput/latency verification.

Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Morgan <danielle@brightdesk.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luke Harper <luke.harper@brightdesk.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T15:31:00Z
Subject: RE: Discovery follow-up — fit benchmarks, toolcall retries & JSON contract plan

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Appreciate the clear plan. A few follow-ups from our side: 

1) Sample data — we'll send an anonymized 1k set by EOD today (csv export). Expect the file to include: ticket_text, customer_metadata (hashed id), current_tags.
2) JSON contract: thanks for the draft. Two asks: can the contract include an explicit "confidence_score" float (0.0-1.0) and an optional "explainability_trace" array for audit? The latter can be empty in the first run.
3) Retries/latency: 300ms p95 is tight for us at scale — how aggressive is the retry backoff? If a retry adds >50ms we might prefer a single-call fallback rule.
4) Security: we'll need confirmation that model inputs are not persisted beyond 30 days and that key rotation is supported.

We'll accept the 30-min sync after you share the fit_benchmark_report_q4.pdf. Please share the Drive link.

Best,
Danielle
Head of Product — BrightDesk

----
On 2026-12-06 09:08, Monica Patel wrote:
> Thanks Vivek — adding a couple of operational checks we'll run during the fit...

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Morgan <danielle@brightdesk.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Luke Harper <luke.harper@brightdesk.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Discovery follow-up — fit benchmarks, toolcall retries & JSON contract plan

Thanks — quick clarifications and next steps.

1) JSON contract: we'll add "confidence_score" as a top-level float and include an optional "explainability_trace" list. We'll update json_contract_v1.yaml and push json_contract_v2.yaml to the Drive by noon PST.
2) Retries: baseline retry plan: up to 2 retries for transient parser/model errors with exponential backoff (60ms -> 120ms). If your latency budget is very strict we can switch to a conservative policy (0 retries + immediate fallback to rule-based tagger). We should decide per-route — the Redwood Console can apply per-route policies so critical/high-SLA routes have no retries.
3) Data retention & security: confirm we will not persist inputs beyond 30 days by default for this pilot. Key rotation: supported via KMS integration (we'll share the KMS onboarding checklist).

Deliverables being uploaded now: fit_benchmark_report_q4.pdf, updated prompt-set with annotations, and json_contract_v2.yaml. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-fitbench (same as above).

Proposed follow-up: book 30 min on Thursday 12/9 10:00-10:30 PST to review the 1k fit and agree on the 10k run window. If that works please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
